source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: STACK Infrastructure operates its Portland-market campus in Hillsboro, Oregon, one of ten Americas markets for the Denver, Colorado-headquartered data center developer and operator, which describes itself company-wide as running roughly 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 global markets in the Americas, Asia Pacific, and EMEA regions. Hillsboro sits within the greater Portland metro area and has become one of the Pacific Northwest's established data center corridors, drawing operators including Google, Digital Realty, and Infomart in addition to STACK, owing to relatively affordable and largely hydroelectric-sourced power, favorable state and local tax treatment including property tax abatement programs, and proximity to trans-Pacific subsea cable landings that give the region low-latency connectivity to Asia. This specific building, POR01A, is one of two buildings making up STACK's POR01 campus, an 18-acre site with 40 megawatts of current IT capacity and 36 additional megawatts of disclosed future expansion capacity. POR01A itself is the smaller of the two buildings at 5 megawatts of capacity across 65,000 square feet, while its companion building POR01B carries 36 megawatts across 215,000 square feet. STACK markets the Portland campus generally toward cloud providers and other large-scale digital infrastructure customers, citing the region's renewable energy access and minimal natural disaster risk, though as is standard across the colocation and build-to-suit industry, STACK does not publicly name its tenants at this or any other site. STACK's own published materials do not disclose a street address, a year of completion, the responsible power utility, or any Tier certification for POR01A specifically, and no independent local news coverage of this building's permitting, tax abatement terms, or utility interconnection could be located this session. Those gaps are recorded here rather than filled with invented detail.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR01 campus in Hillsboro occupies 65,000 square feet of technical space but has not published a megawatt capacity figure, making it impossible to assess power delivery density or total IT load.

The operator's Portland page describes two distinct buildings on an 18-acre campus with different capacities, yet lists only one row in this registry. The published 65,000 square feet matches the smaller building's footprint exactly, but without a paired megawatt figure, the space measurement alone cannot answer whether this facility is sized for AI workloads or general enterprise hosting. Among Oregon's 133 mapped facilities, only six publish power capacity at all, so missing data here is typical rather than exceptional.

For buyers evaluating AI infrastructure, floor area is a necessary starting point but insufficient without power density and uptime certifications. The operator has released neither here. A 65,000-square-foot building could be fully powered for dense GPU work or could be a shell awaiting infrastructure. The data does not distinguish between these cases, and no public certifications are listed to indicate redundancy or compliance standards that AI customers typically require.
